title: Clock synchronisation
summary: Synchronise the clocks of all ICT systems to the NTP servers of NIC or NPL, or to servers traceable to them. Entities spread across jurisdictions may use other accurate time sources that do not drift from these.
typical_evidence: NTP configuration (cloud time sync settings; chrony or ntpd config; endpoint time policy) showing the source

title: Report cyber incidents within 6 hours
summary: Report the incident types listed in Annexure I to CERT-In within 6 hours of noticing them or being told of them. The types include targeted scanning; compromise of critical systems; unauthorised access; defacement; malicious code; attacks on servers; phishing; DoS and DDoS; attacks on applications, IoT, cloud, digital payment systems and social media accounts; data breaches and data leaks.
typical_evidence: Incident response procedure with a CERT-In reporting step and 6-hour clock; reporting template; records of reports made in the period

title: Point of contact
summary: Designate a point of contact to interface with CERT-In and share their details with CERT-In in the prescribed format; keep it current.
typical_evidence: POC designation record; submission to CERT-In; current contact details

title: Provide information on CERT-In orders
summary: When CERT-In orders information or assistance for cyber incident response or prevention, provide it within the time given in the order.
typical_evidence: Procedure for handling CERT-In orders; owner named

title: Logs kept 180 days within India
summary: Enable logs of all ICT systems and keep them securely for a rolling 180 days within Indian jurisdiction; provide them to CERT-In with incident reports or on order.
typical_evidence: Log retention settings (>=180 days) for cloud audit logs; application and network logs; log storage region in India

title: Subscriber records for DC, VPS, cloud and VPN providers
summary: Data centres, VPS providers, cloud service providers and VPN service providers must register and keep accurate subscriber information (validated names, period of hire, IPs allotted, email, address, contact numbers, purpose, ownership pattern) for 5 years after cancellation.
typical_evidence: Only if the company is such a provider: KYC and subscriber data retention procedure; sample records

title: Records for virtual asset service providers
summary: Virtual asset service providers, exchanges and custodian wallet providers must keep KYC and financial transaction records for 5 years.
typical_evidence: Only if the company is a VASP: KYC records; transaction record retention
